one_month_reasoning: AMD has not announced its Q3 2026 report date: its IR press-release list as of 2026-09-30 ends with the World Labs deal (Sep 28) and EDGAR shows no newer 8-K. Nov 3 is only an estimate from past schedules; 2 of the last 5 Q3 reports (Oct 26 2021, Oct 29 2024) fell before an Oct-30 cutoff, so I now put ~28% on the print (and Q4 guide) landing inside the window, rather than treating it as certainly outside. Also in the window: the Oct 27-28 FOMC after the Sep-16 25bp hike, TSMC's mid-October results, and late-October hyperscaler Q3 reports with capex guidance (Meta and Microsoft are named Helios customers). I have no directional edge on these: Q3 was guided to $13.0B +/- $0.3B and Helios shipments were to start late in Q3, so a beat is likely but largely expected at ~39x FY27 EPS near the 52-week high. I use a mixture: 72% a lognormal centred at ~$606 with monthly sigma ~19.4% (72% realized vol / ~3.7), 28% the same plus a ~10% earnings-day jump. This leaves the median near spot (P(>=604.09) = 0.503) and fattens both tails by 0.5-1pp.

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) 30x a Sep-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS of ~$20.4 (0.25 x FY27 consensus $15.58 + 0.75 x FY28 est ~$22) less ~4.2% expected dilution from first-GW warrant tranches and World Labs shares (~$590, 60% weight) and (b) management's long-term EPS path (~$30 by 2030 at a 25x exit, discounted 3 years at 11%, plus ~$6/share net cash, ~$555, 40% weight) = ~$580. The supervisor's checks confirmed each input; the lease guarantees ($4.1B maximum, ~$2.5/share) go into the bear case, not the base value.

bear.story: AI capex digestion in 2027 or a slower Helios/MI450 ramp (the ramp pace is the risk, not the denied Feb-2026 slip report); the first-GW deployments (Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta) land late or smaller, and customers lean on AMD for financing: the 10-Q shows up to $4.1B of guarantees on commercial partners' data-center leases (up to 15 years, may be issued in exchange for warrants) alongside $30.3B of purchase commitments that could become inventory risk. Memory costs squeeze client. EPS ~$12-13 at ~25x.

base.story: DC roughly doubles in 2027 as guided, FY27 EPS ~$15-17, the Street moves to FY28 EPS ~$21-22 and the multiple compresses to ~30x; some warrant dilution. The stock grinds sideways-to-up from an already full price.

bull.story: Helios ramps ahead of plan; revenue per GW in the double-digit billions across 3+ multi-GW customers pushes FY27 EPS toward the $20 high estimate and FY28 toward $28-30, with the market holding ~35x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$380 the stock would trade at ~24x FY27 consensus EPS ($15.58) and ~17x a ~$22 FY28 path, roughly a market multiple for a company guiding DC to more than double. That would most likely mean the 2027 Helios/MI450 ramp or the multi-GW customer commitments (OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic) have slipped or been cut, or that customer financing stress has hit (lease guarantees called, commitments deferred), not ordinary volatility. It is ~37% below today, about one annual sigma of a de-risked 55-60% vol. The supervisor puts it at $400 (~26x FY27); I keep $380 because in AMD's 72%-vol tape a 34% drawdown can come from a sector multiple reset alone, as it did in 2022, without a broken company thesis.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks confirmed my round-1 inputs (FY27 consensus $15.58 from 50 analysts, Helios in production with shipments from late Q3 and step-ups in Q4 and Q1'27, net cash ~$9.9B, ~4-5% expected dilution), so fair value stays ~$580: rising earnings offset by de-rating from ~39x FY27 to ~30x forward and ~4% dilution. It corrected two points and added one fact, all of which I verified in the 10-Q (Q2 2026). First, my claim that the $600 Meta threshold being met removed the brake on vesting was overstated: tranches vest on GPU purchase milestones and must then meet further technical and commercial conditions, so dilution tracks GW shipments. That changes the wording but not my ~55M expected shares. Second, the 10-Q shows up to $4.1B of lease guarantees for commercial partners (up to 15 years, 'may be issued in exchange for warrants'). That is only ~$2.5/share at maximum exposure, but together with the $30.3B purchase commitments it shows AMD taking on customer credit risk, which I add to the bear story; I leave the bear probability at 25% because the exposure is small relative to value. Third, the Q3 date is not confirmed (no IR release or 8-K as of Sep 30), so the 1-month ladder now carries a ~28% chance of an in-window print plus the Oct 27-28 FOMC, which widens both tails by 0.5-1pp. I keep the 12-month ladder unchanged: median ~$612, log-sigma 0.60, P(>=604) 0.51. The supervisor's ladder sits within ~1-3pp of mine (it is a little thinner in the right tail), and nothing it found moves the centre or the tails beyond noise, so I see no reason to shade toward it. Scenarios are unchanged at 25/50/25 ($330/$640/$950). I keep the thesis break at $380 against the supervisor's $400 (see the thesis_break_reason). Research this round: 4 fetches of primary sources (10-Q, EDGAR 8-K list, AMD IR releases).
